newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN BROADCASTING CORP MIDDAY UPDATE.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN BROADCASTING CORP MIDDAY UPDATE.

text.p: COSTELLO WARNS STATES NOT TO DOUBLE DIP ON TAXES
Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has warned State Governments they must refund all petrol, alcohol and tobacco taxes paid in advance, before they are entitled to Commonwealth assistance.
State Treasury officials are meeting in Sydney today to try to sort out the confusion following the High Court ruling that $5 billion worth of state taxes are unconstitutional.
Liquor and tobacco wholesalers are threatening to raise prices unless governments refund taxes already paid.
Mr Costello said the Federal Government's rescue package was clearly conditional on the refunds being made and prices remaining stable.
He said states would not be allowed to hang on to the taxes and expect the Commonwealth to repay them.
MAN SHOT IN DARLING HARBOUR DRAMA
One man is dead and another wounded in a shooting incident at Sydney's Darling Harbour.
The incident, which happened near the Convention Centre Mall, apparently involved an attempted robbery.
Initial reports were sketchy, but a store manager said a security guard had been collecting shop takings.
On the way to the bank, he was attacked and hit over the head. The guard then shot his attacker dead, the shop manager said.
The area has been sealed off and police have been tight-lipped about the incident.
MAN ACCUSED OF JAIDYN LESKIE'S MURDER SEEKS BAIL
The man accused of murdering missing toddler Jaidyn Leskie is seeking bail in the Victorian Supreme Court.
Greg Domaszewicz, 29, of Newborough, was charged with the 14-month-old's murder late last month.
Jaidyn was reported missing from Mr Domaszewicz's home in the early hours of June 15.
His body has not been found despite an intensive 20-day search by police.
Counsel for Mr Domaszewicz, John Lee, said bail should be granted because of exceptional circumstances which included fresh evidence.
RESEARCHERS TAKE SNAPSHOT OF GREAT BARRIER REEF
The Great Barrier Reef is having a health check-up as part of the International Year of the Reef.
The Marine Park Authority and the Queensland Department of Environment will work together with volunteers, scientists and the tourism industry to assess the reef.
Conservation officer Stephanie Golden said more than 35 countries would pool their results to assemble a snapshot of the state of the world's reefs.
She said the researchers might also check on the number of crown of thorns starfish.
